description: This app's own two commands, plus scoped doors: the window may ask the OS to open the project's issue tracker and the three Calibre and Kindle Previewer download pages the KFX checklist links to, and to ask the updater plugin to check, download and install. The updater grant has no allow-list to write; its scope is the one endpoint in tauri.conf.json. Three bare grants besides the doors: process:allow-restart, so the window can restart itself after an update once the engine is idle (the plugin's exit is not granted); core:window:allow-start-dragging, so the strip along the top of the page, and the gaps in the tab bar, can move it; and dialog:allow-open, so the window can show a native folder picker and hand the path it returns to the engine, nothing more, with no allow-list to write because the OS dialog the user picks in is the scope. The shell plugin is still used only from Rust; the dialog plugin's open is now used by the window too, for that one picker. See ADR 2026-09-21: doors, not commands. The window no longer reveals a file itself: the engine's own reveal verb does that now, per the ADR's amendment.
